evidence.observation:
Splits a page into YAML frontmatter + body using FM_RE (line 36: /^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---?
?/). Missing frontmatter, unparsable YAML, or a non-object result all fall back tolerantly to {type:'other'} with hasFrontmatter=false; a blank/non-string type is also coerced to 'other'. This is the deterministic per-document parse step that yields the type used to derive each document's path, so identical input always yields the same document ID.

Serializes frontmatter + body back into a compliant page. Emits fields in a fixed order (type -> title -> description -> sources -> tags -> timestamp -> passthrough extras), defaults type to 'other', and explicitly never writes the `locked` field. Re-parsing the built page recovers the same type, which the demo asserts via reparse_type.

Splits over-budget source text into chunks. Clamps targetChars to >= 1000 and overlap to [0, floor(target/2)], returns [] for empty input and a single-element array when the trimmed text fits. Otherwise it aggregates splitIntoUnits() output up to the target and prepends the previous chunk's last `overlap` characters, so total chunk characters can exceed the body length. Deterministic for a fixed target.

Produces chunk aggregation units by cutting on markdown heading boundaries (/^#{1,6}\s+\S/), so a semantic section stays whole. Sections exceeding target fall back to blank-line paragraphs, and over-long paragraphs are hard-sliced every `target` chars. This is what makes the demo's multi-section doc split at deterministic points.

Normalizes an entity name/title into a stable slug by scanning characters into alternating CJK and latin/alnum runs: latin runs are lowercased, CJK is preserved verbatim, everything else is a boundary, and runs are joined with hyphens with duplicate/edge hyphens collapsed. Determinism here is what makes the same title map to the same wiki path across ingests (dedup basis).

claims.claim: parseFrontmatter is tolerant and deterministic: documents without a frontmatter block, or with malformed/non-object YAML, resolve to type 'other' rather than throwing, so every corpus file yields a stable document type and path.
buildPage serializes frontmatter with a fixed field order and never emits `locked`; the demo's round-trip check (reparse_type) confirms a built page re-parses to the same type.

chunkText is the deterministic splitter: it clamps targetChars to a minimum of 1000, returns a single chunk when the text fits, and otherwise aggregates heading-aligned units with an overlap tail, so chunk counts and chunk lengths are reproducible run to run.

splitIntoUnits cuts on markdown heading boundaries first and only falls back to paragraph/hard splits for over-long sections, which is why the demo's long multi-heading document splits into 2 chunks at a deterministic boundary.

slugify + pageRelPath turn each page's (type, title) into a deterministic repository-relative path (e.g. entity/'Redis Cluster' -> wiki/entities/redis-cluster.md), which the demo hashes with sha256 to a stable 16-hex-character document ID.

conclusion: The wiki-ingest helpers were demoed end-to-end on a 4-file local markdown corpus (.prale-eval/demo/corpus). The real slug.ts and chunker.ts modules are imported directly (Node 24 native TypeScript type stripping); frontmatter.ts's only runtime dependency (`yaml`) is not installed in this checkout, so the frontmatter behaviors it contributes to the demo are provided by a behavior-equivalent local mirror, documented as a limitation. The demo produces deterministic output: 4 documents, stable 16-hex document IDs derived from each page's slug-based relative path, and 5 total chunks (redis-cluster.md splits into 2 chunks of 988/602 chars on a heading boundary; the other three documents fit in 1 chunk each). Two consecutive runs produce byte-identical out.json, confirming determinism.

validation.notes: Node v24.14.0. Demo executed successfully and printed a deterministic summary. Limitation: the `yaml` package required by MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/ingest-v2/frontmatter.ts is not installed (no node_modules in this checkout, and installing dependencies was out of scope), so frontmatter.ts could not be imported directly; a behavior-equivalent local mirror of parseFrontmatter/isLocked/readSources/buildPage was used instead, and slug.ts/chunker.ts were imported and executed as the real modules. Determinism was verified by running the demo twice and diffing out.json (identical). No test runner (vitest) was available either, so validation is the demo run rather than the repo's unit tests.
